figs.title: Curved beam stress distribution
figs.caption: In a curved beam the fibre strain varies as (r_n − r)/r, so the bending stress is hyperbolic through the depth. The neutral axis sits a distance e from the centroid toward the centre of curvature, and the inner fibre carries more stress than the straight beam value Mc/I.

figs.title: Axial load moves the neutral axis
figs.caption: A compressive force adds a uniform −N/A to the linear bending stress My/I, which slides the neutral axis away from the centroid. When N/A equals M/S the neutral axis reaches the extreme fibre and the whole section carries compression.

figs.title: Snap-through versus bifurcation
figs.caption: A shallow truss under load control follows its single path up to the limit point A, where dP/dw = 0, then jumps to the inverted branch. Displacement control traces the falling branch from A to B. At a bifurcation, two distinct equilibrium paths cross at P_cr.

figs.title: Supports as linear and rotational springs
figs.caption: A real joint acts as a translational spring k_v and a rotational spring k_θ at the support. With k_v large, the pin (k_θ = 0) and the clamp (k_θ → ∞) are the two limits, and the prop reaction moves from wL/2 to 3wL/8 as k_θ grows.
